newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Three stowaways found dead on ship in Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: Three stowaways found dead on ship in Ivory Coast.

text.p: Three Africans who tried to stowaway in a cocoa ship from Ivory Coast to the United States died after the crew fumigated the hold in line with export regulations, police and port sources said on Wednesday.
Four other would-be stowaways were pulled from the hold of the Gibralter-flagged Rizcun on Friday after the crew heard them knocking on the hatch-covers, the sources told Reuters.
The nationalities of the would-be stowaways were not immediately clear. The survivors spoke English or French.
"Three were found dead on Saturday and Sunday. They must have inhaled the toxic fumes," Abidjan port Chief Police Commissioner Camara Yaya said.

"The men got on board in Ivory Coast without the knowledge of the crew and hid in the ship's holds as it loaded cocoa," he added. "About five others were caught after escaping and taken to a clinic. They are lucky to be alive."
The crew set off phosphate-based fumigation bombs in sealed holds to comply with phytosanitary rules as the ship prepared to leave for Philadelphia with 10,000 tonnes of cocoa.

A ship surveyor called to the scene said the crew had heard the stowaways beating on sealed hatchcovers, adding that a search party with gas masks hunted for other survivors but could only make short forays into each hold.
"People are not supposed to go into holds until 62 hours after fumigation," he said.
Shipping sources say hundreds of stowaways are reported in Ivory Coast each year.
